title: Asato Ma Sadgamaya | Yajurveda mantra with meaning
desc: Yajurveda, Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.3.28: the mantra in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how it is used.
caption: Yajurveda, Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.3.28
intro: This is a mantra from the **Yajurveda** (Yajurveda, Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.3.28). Below are the Sanskrit text and a **plain English meaning**.
takeaways: The four Vedas are Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda.
Vedic mantras are learned by listening and repeating.

p: **असतो मा सद्गमय । तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय । मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय ॥ ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥**
Lead me from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to immortality.
The Yajurveda is one of the four Vedas, the oldest scriptures of Sanatana Dharma, handed down by voice for thousands of years.

faq.a: Lead me from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to immortality.
There are **four**: Rig, Yajur, Sama and Atharva.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering.
